newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Thousands acclaim Romania's king in Bucharest.
newsitem.headline: Thousands acclaim Romania's king in Bucharest.

text.p: Thousands of chanting well-wishers acclaimed Romania's exiled King Michael on Friday, visiting his homeland a week after the new centrist government restored his citizenship.

Michael, weary but beaming, waved to up 20,000 people shouting "King Michael!" and "King and Country" in University Square, where dozens of demonstrators died in the December 1989 upheaval that toppled Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.

Michael, 75, shook hands with hundreds of well-wishers and mounted first a pedestal honouring the 1989 dead and then the back of a car alongside his wife Ana of Bourbon Parma. But he abandoned an attempt to address the crowd through a megaphone.
Many people had yellowing portraits of the king pinned to their lapels. Students hung out of windows overlooking the square. The crowd later dispersed without incident.

The king's visit, his second to Romania since the fall of communism, is officially described as private, though his programme includes meetings with President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
Romania's new leadership hope to use the prestige of the king, forced to abdicate by pro-Moscow communists in 1947, to promote their longshot bid to win early entry to NATO.
